== Biography ==
Peter was born in 1740.  He passed away in 1812.

Erected by JOHN and JAMES GLASGOW in MEMORY of PETER GLASGOW their father, late Tenant Whitebank, who died the 7th Novr. 1812, aged 72 years.
Also JEAN ANDERSON his Spouse, who died 7 Jan. 1809, aged 73 years.
THREE of their Children, who died young.
== Research Notes ==
=== Whitebank trial identification — 30 October 2026 ===
The trial index names Peter Glasgow of Whitebank, tried on 9 October 1797. The held memorial transcription for Peter Glasgow-2878 calls him the late tenant of Whitebank, records death on 7 November 1812 aged 72, names Jean Anderson as spouse, and sons John and James as erectors. Matching personal name and the specific tenancy provide a substantially better identification than the Bathgate Peter-1466 comparison, which has no Whitebank link. Prefer Peter-2878 as the trial subject at 94% subjective identity confidence. This is one memorial, also indexed under Jean, not two independent witnesses.

The original memorial image and court papers were not newly inspected. The trial index gives no age, family or occupation; another Peter of the same holding remains possible. The index records a guilty verdict and transportation sentence, not proof of a voyage, destination, actual removal, return or pardon. Do not use this occurrence to infer either man’s parents, alter Peter-1466’s 79% father assessment, or transfer the unassigned 1818 Edinburgh burial. Reassessment of held memorial evidence combined with a fresh index read, not newly discovered court papers.<ref name="WhitebankTrial1797">[https://www.scottishindexes.com/jcdetail.aspx?jcid=1797040&pid=179704079 Scottish Indexes, High Court of Justiciary Trial Papers], Peter Glasgow of Whitebank, 9 October 1797, NRS JC26/1797/40; index checked 30 October 2026. Original court papers not inspected.</ref><ref name="WhitebankMemorial">[https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/198800998/peter_glasgow Peter Glasgow memorial 198800998] and [https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/198800999/jean-glasgow Jean Anderson memorial 198800999], held transcription of one shared Stichill stone, not two witnesses. The stone calls Peter the late tenant of Whitebank; original photograph not newly inspected.</ref>
